gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-038.prompt: Harlow County replaced its paper parking permits with a phone app. In the first year, parking-fine revenue fell 30%. The county treasurer concludes that drivers are obeying parking rules far more often under the app system. Which of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the treasurer's conclusion?

options.a: The app lets drivers extend a session without returning to the car.
options.b: The county did not change the size of its parking fines that year.
options.c: Most drivers in the county downloaded the app within two months.
options.d: The county cut its number of parking inspectors in half that year.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-038.explanation: Fewer fines can come from fewer violations or from fewer tickets written. Halving the inspector force explains the revenue drop without any change in driver behavior, so it undercuts the compliance conclusion.

distractorExplanations.a: Remote extensions give a mechanism for better compliance, so this supports the treasurer.
distractorExplanations.c: Fast adoption says nothing about whether rule-breaking fell; if anything it fits the treasurer's story.
distractorExplanations.b: Unchanged fine amounts rule out one alternative explanation, which strengthens the conclusion.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-041.prompt: A bakery chain found that its stores with self-service kiosks sell 12% more pastries per customer than its stores without kiosks. Managers plan to install kiosks in every store to raise pastry sales. The managers' plan assumes which of the following?

options.a: Customers generally prefer kiosks to ordering from a cashier.
options.b: Kiosks cost less to run than hiring additional cashiers.
options.c: Pastries are the most profitable product the chain sells.
options.d: The kiosks, rather than other store traits, cause the extra sales.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-041.explanation: The plan moves from a correlation (kiosk stores sell more) to a cause (kiosks raise sales). If the extra sales came from location or store size instead, adding kiosks elsewhere would not help, so the plan needs this assumption.

distractorExplanations.a: Customers could dislike kiosks and still buy more pastries through them; a general preference is not required.
distractorExplanations.b: Cost matters for profit, but the plan's goal is higher pastry sales, not lower labor costs.
distractorExplanations.c: The plan aims to raise pastry sales whether or not pastries are the top-margin item.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-047.prompt: After Lakeside City installed brighter streetlights on its main avenue, reported nighttime car accidents on that avenue rose, even though drivers could now see much better. Which of the following, if true, best explains this result?

options.a: Most accidents on the avenue happen during daytime hours.
options.b: The new streetlights use less electricity than the old ones did.
options.c: Accidents on other city streets declined over the same period.
options.d: Drivers began traveling noticeably faster on the newly lit avenue.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-047.explanation: Better visibility should reduce accidents, so the rise needs a factor that offsets it. If drivers responded to the brighter road by speeding up, the added risk from speed can outweigh the visibility gain.

distractorExplanations.b: Energy use has no connection to how many accidents occur.
distractorExplanations.c: A decline elsewhere makes the rise on the avenue more puzzling, not less.
distractorExplanations.a: The puzzle concerns nighttime accidents; daytime totals do not explain why night crashes rose.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-050.prompt: A school district reports that students who joined its new after-school tutoring program raised their math grades more than students who did not join. The district concludes that the program improves math performance. Which of the following would be most useful to know in evaluating the district's conclusion?

options.a: Whether the program's tutors were certified math teachers
options.b: Whether the district plans to expand the program next year
options.c: How many hours per week the tutoring program met
options.d: Whether students decided on their own to join the program

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-050.explanation: If joining was voluntary, the most motivated students may have signed up, and motivation alone could explain their bigger gains. Knowing how students entered the program tells us whether the comparison isolates the program's effect.

distractorExplanations.a: Tutor credentials might affect quality, but they do not test whether the grade gap was caused by the program at all.
distractorExplanations.c: Meeting hours describe the program; they do not rule out a selection effect.
distractorExplanations.b: Future plans have no bearing on whether the past results show the program works.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-053.prompt: Researchers found that towns with more public libraries per resident have higher adult literacy rates. They argue that access to libraries raises adult literacy. Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the researchers' argument?

options.a: Some towns with no public library have high adult literacy rates.
options.b: Towns with many libraries also tend to have higher average incomes.
options.c: Many library visitors borrow films rather than books or magazines.
options.d: Literacy rates rose in towns soon after new libraries opened there.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-053.explanation: The argument infers cause from a correlation. Showing that literacy rose after libraries opened adds the right time order, which makes it more likely that libraries drove the change rather than the reverse.

distractorExplanations.b: Income is an alternative cause of both libraries and literacy, so this weakens the argument.
distractorExplanations.c: If visitors mostly borrow films, library access is less plausibly the cause of literacy gains.
distractorExplanations.a: High literacy without libraries suggests other causes, which weakens the claim.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-059.prompt: Mayor: Last year, 80% of the complaints our office received were about potholes. Therefore, potholes are the problem that most concerns our city's residents. The mayor's reasoning is most vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that it

options.a: confuses a cause of potholes with one of their effects
options.b: ignores how much pothole repairs will cost the city
options.c: assumes people who complain represent all residents
options.d: treats a minor issue as though it were an emergency

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-059.explanation: Complaints come from a self-selected group. Residents may worry more about crime or housing but not contact the mayor's office about it, so the complaint mix need not reflect what concerns residents most.

distractorExplanations.b: Cost is irrelevant to the claim about what residents care about most.
distractorExplanations.d: The mayor never calls potholes an emergency; the claim is only about relative concern.
distractorExplanations.a: The argument makes no causal claim about potholes.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-062.prompt: All of the interns at Corvell Labs this summer are chemistry majors. Some of the interns received research grants. No one who received a research grant works fewer than 20 hours a week. If the statements above are true, which of the following must also be true?

options.a: Every research grant recipient is a Corvell intern.
options.b: All chemistry majors at Corvell Labs received grants.
options.c: No intern at Corvell Labs works fewer than 20 hours.
options.d: Some chemistry majors work at least 20 hours a week.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-062.explanation: Some interns got grants, and every grant holder works at least 20 hours. Those interns are chemistry majors, so at least some chemistry majors work 20 or more hours a week.

distractorExplanations.b: Only some interns received grants, and nothing is said about every chemistry major.
distractorExplanations.c: Interns without grants could work fewer than 20 hours.
distractorExplanations.a: Grants could also go to people who are not Corvell interns.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-065.prompt: To reduce employee turnover, Brightline Retail plans to raise starting wages by 10%. Exit interviews show that most departing workers cite pay as a reason for leaving. Which of the following, if true, most strongly suggests the plan will fail to reduce turnover?

options.a: Several competitors raised their starting wages 5% last year.
options.b: Brightline's current wages match the average in its region.
options.c: Most departing workers leave for jobs paying at least 25% more.
options.d: Employees also value flexible schedules in addition to pay.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-065.explanation: If leavers are getting raises of 25% or more elsewhere, a 10% increase will not close the gap, so most of them would still leave.

distractorExplanations.b: Average wages do not show whether a 10% raise is enough to keep workers.
distractorExplanations.d: Valuing schedules as well as pay does not show that a pay raise will fail.
distractorExplanations.a: A 10% raise would beat competitors' 5% increases, which supports the plan.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-032.prompt: A city plans to cut downtown traffic congestion by charging drivers a daily fee to enter the central district. Planners expect the fee to reduce car trips into the district by 20%. The planners' expectation depends on which of the following assumptions?

options.a: Other cities have charged congestion fees at a similar price.
options.b: The fee revenue will be spent on public transit improvements.
options.c: Most people who work downtown live outside the central district.
options.d: Many current drivers have a practical alternative to driving in.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-032.explanation: A fee cuts car trips only if drivers can respond by taking transit, carpooling, shifting times, or skipping trips. If nearly everyone must drive in regardless, trips would barely fall.

distractorExplanations.b: Spending the revenue on transit could help, but the expectation can hold even if the money goes elsewhere.
distractorExplanations.c: Where workers live does not settle whether they can avoid driving in.
distractorExplanations.a: Other cities' prices are not required for the fee to work in this city.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-039.prompt: A marine biologist hypothesizes that rising water temperatures, rather than pollution, caused the recent decline of kelp forests along a stretch of coastline. Which of the following, if true, most strongly supports the biologist's hypothesis?

options.a: Kelp forests elsewhere have recovered quickly after storms.
options.b: Pollution along the coastline has risen over the past decade.
options.c: Several fish species depend on kelp forests for shelter.
options.d: Kelp also declined in unpolluted areas where the water warmed.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-039.explanation: The hypothesis sets warming against pollution. A decline where the water warmed but no pollution was present separates the two causes and points to temperature.

distractorExplanations.b: Rising pollution makes the rival explanation more plausible, which weakens the hypothesis.
distractorExplanations.c: The importance of kelp to fish says nothing about why the kelp declined.
distractorExplanations.a: Recovery from storms does not bear on warming versus pollution.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-042.prompt: Sales of electric bicycles in Norhaven doubled last year, yet the number of people who commute by bicycle in the city stayed the same. Which of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy?

options.a: The number of car commuters in Norhaven fell slightly.
options.b: E-bikes cost more than twice as much as regular bicycles.
options.c: Norhaven added many new bicycle lanes the year before.
options.d: Most e-bike buyers replaced a regular bike they already rode.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-042.explanation: If buyers were already cycling to work, they switched bikes without becoming new bicycle commuters. E-bike sales can then double while the number of commuters stays flat.

distractorExplanations.b: Price explains nothing, because sales still doubled.
distractorExplanations.c: New lanes would be expected to raise commuting, which deepens the puzzle.
distractorExplanations.a: Fewer car commuters would suggest more cyclists, which makes the flat count harder to explain.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-048.prompt: A software firm switched to a four-day workweek. Over the next six months, the number of bugs reported in its products fell by 25%. The firm's CEO concludes that the shorter week made engineers more careful. Which of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the CEO's conclusion?

options.a: Other firms with four-day weeks report similar quality gains.
options.b: Engineers said they felt more rested under the new schedule.
options.c: The firm had hired several new engineers the previous year.
options.d: The firm shipped far fewer product updates during those months.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-048.explanation: Fewer releases mean less new code for users to find bugs in. The drop in reported bugs could reflect lower output rather than greater care, which undercuts the CEO's explanation.

distractorExplanations.b: Feeling rested gives a plausible route to more careful work, so this supports the CEO.
distractorExplanations.c: Hiring a year earlier does not explain a drop that began with the schedule change.
distractorExplanations.a: Similar results elsewhere support the CEO's causal claim.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-051.prompt: To attract more younger visitors, a history museum plans to add interactive touchscreen exhibits. Which of the following would be most useful to determine whether the plan is likely to succeed?

options.a: Whether older visitors are satisfied with current exhibits
options.b: Whether touchscreens cost more than printed display panels
options.c: Whether young non-visitors want more interactive exhibits
options.d: Whether nearby museums charge higher admission fees

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-051.explanation: The plan works only if a lack of interactivity is what keeps younger people away. Learning whether young non-visitors want interactive exhibits tests that directly.

distractorExplanations.b: Cost bears on affordability, not on whether the exhibits will attract younger visitors.
distractorExplanations.d: Other museums' prices do not show whether touchscreens will change young people's behavior.
distractorExplanations.a: Older visitors' satisfaction does not show what would draw younger ones.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-054.prompt: In Region X, every farm that grows soybeans also grows corn. Some farms in Region X that grow corn use drip irrigation. No farm in Region X that uses drip irrigation grows wheat. Which of the following can be properly inferred from the statements above?

options.a: No soybean farm in Region X also grows wheat.
options.b: Some soybean farms in Region X use drip irrigation.
options.c: Some corn farms in Region X do not grow any wheat.
options.d: Every corn farm in Region X also grows soybeans.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-054.explanation: Some corn farms use drip irrigation, and no drip-irrigated farm grows wheat. Those corn farms therefore grow no wheat, so some corn farms in Region X do not grow wheat.

distractorExplanations.b: The drip-irrigated corn farms might grow no soybeans at all.
distractorExplanations.d: The statements say soybean farms grow corn, not that corn farms grow soybeans.
distractorExplanations.a: Soybean farms without drip irrigation could grow wheat.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-060.prompt: Critic: The novelist's latest book sold fewer copies than her first book did. Clearly, the quality of her writing has declined. The critic's argument is flawed because it

options.a: draws a conclusion about all novelists from one case
options.b: relies on the opinion of a single book reviewer
options.c: attacks the novelist's character, not her work
options.d: treats sales figures as proof of literary quality

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-060.explanation: Sales depend on marketing, timing, and trends as well as quality. Using a sales drop as proof that the writing got worse assumes sales measure quality.

distractorExplanations.b: No reviewer's opinion is cited; the only evidence is sales.
distractorExplanations.c: The critic says nothing about the novelist's character.
distractorExplanations.a: The conclusion concerns only this novelist.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-063.prompt: Hospital A has a higher death rate among its surgical patients than Hospital B, yet surgeons widely regard Hospital A as the better surgical hospital. Which of the following, if true, best reconciles these facts?

options.a: Hospital A charges more for most surgical procedures.
options.b: Hospital B has more surgeons on its medical staff.
options.c: Hospital A accepts far more high-risk surgical cases.
options.d: Both hospitals perform similar numbers of surgeries.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-063.explanation: If Hospital A takes the sickest, riskiest patients, a higher raw death rate is expected even with better surgical skill. That lets both facts be true together.

distractorExplanations.b: Staff size does not explain why the higher-mortality hospital is rated better.
distractorExplanations.d: Equal volumes rule out one explanation and leave the puzzle unresolved.
distractorExplanations.a: Higher prices do not explain higher mortality or a better reputation.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-066.prompt: Supporters of a proposed ban on single-use plastic shopping bags in Denton argue that it will cut the amount of plastic waste entering the city's landfill. Which of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the supporters' argument?

options.a: Plastic bags are a visible share of Denton's street litter.
options.b: Paper bags cost retailers more to stock than plastic bags do.
options.c: Most Denton shoppers reuse the bags and would buy plastic liners.
options.d: Several nearby towns have debated but not passed such bans.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-066.explanation: If shoppers now reuse store bags as trash liners and would replace them with purchased plastic liners, the plastic still reaches the landfill, possibly in thicker form. The expected waste reduction would shrink or disappear.

distractorExplanations.b: Retailer costs do not affect how much plastic reaches the landfill.
distractorExplanations.d: Other towns' decisions say nothing about the ban's effect in Denton.
distractorExplanations.a: Litter volume suggests the ban addresses a real problem, which does not weaken the landfill claim.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-033.prompt: Eastbrook's transit authority argues that adding express buses on Route 9 will shorten average commute times for Route 9 riders, because express buses make fewer stops. The argument assumes that

options.a: express buses will cost more to run than local buses
options.b: other routes will also receive express service soon
options.c: most Route 9 riders currently drive to work instead
options.d: riders will not face much longer waits for a bus

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-033.explanation: Total commute time includes waiting. If express service meant much longer waits, for example because local buses were cut, the time saved by skipping stops could be lost, so the argument needs waits to stay roughly the same.

distractorExplanations.a: Operating cost does not affect riders' commute times.
distractorExplanations.c: The argument concerns people who ride Route 9, so this contradicts its premise.
distractorExplanations.b: Service on other routes is irrelevant to Route 9 commute times.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-043.prompt: Grantville's public pool began offering free swim lessons for children in 2023. Since then, the number of child drowning incidents in the county has fallen by half. A council member concludes that the lessons caused the decline. Which of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the council member's conclusion?

options.a: The number of drowning incidents among adults did not change.
options.b: Most children who took the lessons can now swim a full length.
options.c: Swim lessons at private clubs in the county cost over $100.
options.d: In 2023 the county also required fences around all private pools.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-043.explanation: A new pool-fencing rule that took effect at the same time is an alternative cause of fewer child drownings. The decline can no longer be credited to the lessons alone.

distractorExplanations.b: Children gaining swimming skill supports the lessons as a cause.
distractorExplanations.c: The price of private lessons does not explain the drop in drownings.
distractorExplanations.a: Unchanged adult drownings suggest the effect was specific to children, which fits the council member's view.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-044.prompt: Researchers argue that a new crop-rotation method, not the unusually wet weather, explains why farms in Valley District produced record wheat yields last year. Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the researchers' argument?

options.a: Most district farmers adopted the method only reluctantly.
options.b: Wheat prices in the district were unusually high last year.
options.c: The method had been tested on only a few farms beforehand.
options.d: Farms that got the same rain but kept old methods saw no gain.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-044.explanation: Comparing farms with the same weather but different methods isolates the method. If the rain-soaked farms that did not change methods saw no gain, the weather cannot explain the record yields.

distractorExplanations.b: Prices affect revenue, not yields.
distractorExplanations.c: Limited prior testing does not show which factor caused last year's yields.
distractorExplanations.a: Farmers' attitudes do not bear on what raised the yields.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-056.prompt: Some argue that remote work harms company culture because employees rarely meet in person. But culture depends mainly on shared goals and fair treatment, not physical proximity. Companies that set clear goals and treat staff fairly can build strong cultures wherever their employees work. Which of the following most accurately expresses the main conclusion of the argument?

options.a: Remote employees rarely meet their coworkers in person.
options.b: Companies should require their employees to work remotely.
options.c: Shared goals matter more to culture than fair treatment.
options.d: Remote work does not have to harm a company's culture.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-056.explanation: The argument rejects the claim that remote work harms culture. Its reasons, that culture rests on goals and fairness and that such firms can thrive anywhere, support the conclusion that remote work need not harm culture.

distractorExplanations.a: This is part of the opposing view the argument responds to.
distractorExplanations.c: The argument treats goals and fairness together; it does not rank them.
distractorExplanations.b: The argument says remote work can succeed, not that it should be required.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-040.prompt: A city reports that since it launched a bike-share program, the number of bicycle accidents has risen by 15%. A council member argues that the program has made cycling in the city more dangerous. Which of the following would be most useful to know in evaluating the council member's argument?

options.a: Whether other cities run similar bike-share programs
options.b: Whether bike-share bikes are heavier than private bikes
options.c: How much the city paid to launch the bike-share program
options.d: Whether the total number of bike trips also increased

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-040.explanation: Danger is about risk per trip. If bike trips rose by more than 15%, the accident rate per trip actually fell and cycling became safer, so total trips are the key missing number.

distractorExplanations.b: Bike weight might matter, but it does not show whether the risk per trip went up.
distractorExplanations.c: Program cost is unrelated to safety.
distractorExplanations.a: Whether other cities have such programs says nothing about risk in this city.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-046.prompt: To boost sales of its store-brand cereal, a grocery chain plans to move the cereal to eye-level shelves, where national brands are now displayed. Which of the following, if true, most strongly suggests the plan could reduce the chain's overall profits?

options.a: The chain sells more cereal on weekends than on weekdays.
options.b: Store-brand cereal costs shoppers less than national brands do.
options.c: Shoppers notice products at eye level more than those on other shelves.
options.d: National brands pay the chain large fees for eye-level shelf space.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-046.explanation: Moving national brands off eye-level shelves could cost the chain the placement fees those brands pay. Lost fees could outweigh any gain from extra store-brand sales.

distractorExplanations.b: A lower shelf price alone does not show that total profit falls.
distractorExplanations.c: Better visibility supports the plan's goal of more store-brand sales.
distractorExplanations.a: The weekly sales pattern is unrelated to shelf placement profits.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-049.prompt: Every vehicle sold by Arlo Motors comes with a three-year warranty. Some vehicles sold by Arlo Motors are electric. Arlo Motors sells vehicles only within the state, and every electric vehicle sold in the state qualifies for a tax credit. If the statements above are true, which of the following must be true?

options.a: Every vehicle sold with a three-year warranty is electric.
options.b: Every vehicle that qualifies for the credit is sold by Arlo Motors.
options.c: Most vehicles sold by Arlo Motors qualify for the tax credit.
options.d: Some vehicles with a three-year warranty qualify for a tax credit.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-049.explanation: Arlo's electric vehicles are sold in the state, so they qualify for the credit, and they carry Arlo's three-year warranty. At least some warrantied vehicles therefore qualify.

distractorExplanations.b: Other dealers' electric vehicles sold in the state also qualify.
distractorExplanations.c: Only some Arlo vehicles are known to be electric, not most.
distractorExplanations.a: Arlo's non-electric vehicles also carry the warranty.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-058.prompt: An online poll on a cycling-enthusiast website found that 85% of respondents support building more bike lanes in the city. The site's editor concludes that most city residents support more bike lanes. The editor's reasoning is flawed because it

options.a: confuses support for bike lanes with actual cycling
options.b: fails to state how much new bike lanes would cost
options.c: assumes that bike lanes reduce traffic accidents
options.d: relies on a sample unlikely to represent city residents

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-058.explanation: Visitors to a cycling site are far more likely than typical residents to favor bike lanes, and some may not live in the city. The poll cannot support a claim about most residents.

distractorExplanations.b: Cost is irrelevant to the claim about residents' support.
distractorExplanations.c: The argument makes no claim about accidents.
distractorExplanations.a: The argument discusses support only; it does not mention how much people cycle.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-061.prompt: When a regional airline cut its fares by 20%, its total revenue increased, even though it did not add any flights. Which of the following, if true, best explains this outcome?

options.a: The airline's older planes had higher maintenance costs.
options.b: Fuel prices rose sharply during the same period of time.
options.c: The fare cut filled many seats that had previously flown empty.
options.d: Business travelers make up most of the airline's passengers.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-061.explanation: Revenue is price times seats sold. If lower fares filled many previously empty seats, the rise in passengers can outweigh the 20% price cut, even on the same flights.

distractorExplanations.b: Fuel prices affect costs, not revenue.
distractorExplanations.d: Business travelers are typically less price-sensitive, which makes a revenue gain from a fare cut less likely.
distractorExplanations.a: Maintenance is a cost and does not explain higher revenue.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-064.prompt: A town replaced its streetlights with motion-activated LED lights, and the town's electricity bill for street lighting fell by 40%. The public works director attributes the savings to the new lights. Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the director's claim?

options.a: The LED lights cost more to buy than the old streetlights.
options.b: Some residents said the new lights switch on too slowly.
options.c: Neighboring towns are weighing similar lighting projects.
options.d: The town's electricity rate stayed the same over the period.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-064.explanation: A lower bill could come from a lower price per kilowatt-hour. If the rate stayed the same, the drop must reflect less electricity used, which points to the new lights.

distractorExplanations.b: Complaints about response time do not bear on energy savings.
distractorExplanations.c: Other towns' plans do not show what caused this town's savings.
distractorExplanations.a: Purchase price concerns up-front cost, not the drop in the electricity bill.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-067.prompt: Trellis Publishing plans to raise its profits by releasing its textbooks only as e-books rather than in print, since e-books cost far less to produce and distribute. The plan assumes that

options.a: print textbooks are heavier than most students like
options.b: most authors now prefer to write for digital formats
options.c: e-book revenue will not fall far below current print revenue
options.d: competitors will soon stop printing their textbooks

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-067.explanation: Lower costs raise profit only if revenue does not drop by more than the savings. If students bought far fewer e-books, or paid much less for them, profits could fall.

distractorExplanations.b: Authors' preferences do not determine whether profits rise.
distractorExplanations.d: The plan can work whatever competitors do.
distractorExplanations.a: Student complaints about weight are not required for lower costs to raise profit.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-065-du.prompt: Over the past five years, average test scores at Pineview High have risen steadily. The principal credits the school's block-scheduling system, which was introduced five years ago. Which of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the principal's argument?

options.a: Scores dipped slightly in the first semester after the change.
options.b: Teachers at Pineview prefer block scheduling to the old system.
options.c: Several nearby schools still use traditional daily schedules.
options.d: Pineview began admitting students by entrance exam that same year.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-065-du.explanation: Admitting students by entrance exam at the same time would raise the academic level of the student body. That alternative cause explains higher scores without block scheduling.

distractorExplanations.b: Teacher preference does not show whether the schedule raised scores.
distractorExplanations.c: Without score data for those schools, this neither helps nor hurts the argument.
distractorExplanations.a: A brief early dip followed by steady gains is consistent with the principal's claim.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-066-du.prompt: Although the number of registered voters in Ashford rose by 10% between two elections, the number of votes cast fell. Which of the following, if true, most helps to explain this?

options.a: Most registered voters in Ashford own the homes they live in.
options.b: Ashford's population grew by about 8% over the same period.
options.c: Ashford added two polling stations before the later election.
options.d: The later election had no contested races for major offices.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-066-du.explanation: Turnout depends on how much is at stake. With no contested major races, many registered voters had little reason to vote, so fewer votes can be cast even from a larger pool.

distractorExplanations.b: Population growth fits the rise in registration but does not explain fewer votes.
distractorExplanations.c: More polling stations should make voting easier, which deepens the puzzle.
distractorExplanations.a: Home ownership says nothing about why turnout fell between the two elections.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-067-du.prompt: Economist: When a country's currency weakens, its exports become cheaper for foreign buyers and its imports become more expensive at home. Last year, the Delan currency weakened sharply against all major currencies. Which of the following is most strongly supported by the economist's statements?

options.a: Foreign buyers now prefer Delan goods to their own goods.
options.b: Delan's total exports must have risen during last year.
options.c: Delan's government deliberately weakened its currency.
options.d: Imported goods likely became costlier for Delan residents.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-067-du.explanation: The economist states that a weaker currency makes imports more expensive at home. Since Delan's currency weakened sharply, imports likely cost Delan residents more.

distractorExplanations.b: Cheaper exports make higher export volume plausible, but other factors could prevent it, so it need not have happened.
distractorExplanations.c: The statements say nothing about why the currency weakened.
distractorExplanations.a: Lower prices do not establish a general preference for Delan goods.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-057.prompt: A company's HR department found that employees who attend its optional wellness seminars take fewer sick days than employees who do not. HR proposes making the seminars mandatory to reduce sick days company-wide. Which of the following, if true, most seriously undermines the proposal?

options.a: Sick-day rates differ widely across company offices.
options.b: The seminars take place during paid working hours.
options.c: The employees who attend now are healthier to begin with.
options.d: Outside speakers lead most of the seminar sessions.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-057.explanation: If already-healthy employees choose to attend, health explains both attendance and fewer sick days. Forcing everyone to attend would not give other employees that underlying health.

distractorExplanations.b: Scheduling during work hours does not show the seminars fail to reduce sick days.
distractorExplanations.d: Who leads the sessions is irrelevant to whether they reduce absences.
distractorExplanations.a: Variation across offices does not address whether seminars cause fewer sick days.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-034.prompt: Harbor Mutual, a coastal insurer, raised premiums by 15% on homes within one mile of the shoreline, citing higher flood risk. Harbor predicts that its profits from those policies will rise. The prediction relies on the assumption that

options.a: the shoreline will not move over the next decade
options.b: flood risk is lower for homes farther from the shore
options.c: most coastal homes were built before building codes
options.d: few affected homeowners will switch to another insurer

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-034.explanation: Higher premiums raise profit only if most customers stay. If many homeowners switched insurers, the lost policies could outweigh the higher price per policy.

distractorExplanations.b: The prediction concerns shoreline policies; risk elsewhere is not required.
distractorExplanations.c: The age of homes is not needed for the profit prediction.
distractorExplanations.a: A moving shoreline over a decade is not needed for near-term profit from higher premiums.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-035.prompt: Many people assume that raising the speed limit on rural highways will increase fatal accidents. Yet after Kestrel State raised its rural limit, highway deaths there fell, apparently because drivers were less frustrated and passed other cars less often. So higher speed limits do not always make highways more dangerous. In the argument, the claim that highway deaths in Kestrel State fell plays which of the following roles?

options.a: It is a prediction that the argument ends up rejecting.
options.b: It is the main conclusion that the argument draws.
options.c: It is an assumption the argument tries to disprove.
options.d: It is evidence offered against a common assumption.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-035.explanation: The argument opens with the common belief that higher limits raise fatalities, then cites Kestrel State's falling deaths to challenge it. The final sentence is the conclusion; the fall in deaths is evidence for it.

distractorExplanations.b: The conclusion is the final sentence, that higher limits do not always make highways more dangerous.
distractorExplanations.c: The argument accepts the fall in deaths as fact; the belief it disputes is the common assumption.
distractorExplanations.a: The fall in deaths is reported as an observed result, not a prediction.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-045.prompt: Archaeologists found charred barley grains at a site dated to 9,000 years ago and concluded that people there farmed barley rather than gathering it wild. Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the archaeologists' conclusion?

options.a: Nearby sites contain stone tools for grinding grain.
options.b: Wild barley grew widely in the region at that time.
options.c: Charred grains survive far longer than uncharred ones.
options.d: The grains show traits found only in cultivated barley.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-045.explanation: The question is whether the barley was farmed or gathered wild. Traits found only in domesticated barley directly show cultivation.

distractorExplanations.b: Abundant wild barley makes gathering more plausible, which weakens the conclusion.
distractorExplanations.c: Better preservation explains why grains were found, not whether they were farmed.
distractorExplanations.a: People ground wild grain too, so grinding tools do not separate farming from gathering.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-022.prompt: For decades, the standard approach to conserving endangered species has been to protect their habitats. However, a new study suggests that for species with extremely small and fragmented populations, this strategy alone may be insufficient. The study argues that in such cases, direct intervention, such as captive breeding programs and reintroduction to new, protected areas, is often necessary to prevent extinction. The reasoning is that small, isolated populations are highly vulnerable to random environmental fluctuations and genetic drift, which can lead to a rapid decline even in a seemingly secure habitat. The study's argument depends on which of the following assumptions?

options.a: Captive breeding costs less than protecting a habitat.
options.b: Habitat protection fails for species with large populations.
options.c: Reintroduced species never disrupt their new ecosystems.
options.d: Direct intervention can offset the risks of genetic drift.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-022.explanation: The study recommends direct intervention because small populations face random fluctuations and genetic drift. That recommendation only makes sense if intervention can actually reduce those risks; if it cannot, the case for it collapses.

distractorExplanations.a: The study argues intervention is necessary, not cheaper; cost is not part of its reasoning.
distractorExplanations.b: The study is limited to small, fragmented populations and says nothing about habitat protection failing for large ones.
distractorExplanations.c: The argument does not need reintroduction to be harmless in every case, only to help prevent extinction.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-023.prompt: A recent survey found that employees who regularly use standing desks report significantly higher levels of job satisfaction and fewer instances of back pain compared to those who use traditional sitting desks. The survey concluded that companies should invest in standing desks to improve employee well-being and productivity. Which of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the survey's conclusion?

options.a: Employees who are already more health-conscious or proactive about their well-being might be more likely to choose standing desks.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-024.prompt: The city of Veridia has seen a significant increase in its deer population over the past decade, leading to more deer-related traffic accidents and damage to residential gardens. In response, the city council proposed a plan to reintroduce natural predators, such as wolves, into a large, forested area bordering the city. Proponents argue this will naturally control the deer population without resorting to culling or fencing. Which of the following, if true, casts the most serious doubt on the plan's likely effectiveness?

options.a: The proposed forested area is significantly smaller than the historical range required to support a viable wolf population.
options.d: In other regions, reintroduced wolves reduced deer numbers within five years.

distractorExplanations.d: Evidence that wolves reduced deer elsewhere supports the plan rather than casting doubt on it.
